extDesc.message: Steam revenue calculator: units sold, net revenue and wishlists on any store page. Sourced ranges, not fake precision. Free.

legendGood.message: Two methods admit a common figure, on a game the sources measured
legendGood.description: Deliberately says nothing about the band being narrow, and nothing about the answer being close. Band width no longer scores, and the grade has not been shown to predict accuracy. See the Confidence section of docs/METHODOLOGY.md.

legendFair.message: One method only, a near miss between bands, or a cross-check objecting

legendLow.message: Methods contradict, or the sources never measured a game this size — read the range, not the midpoint

rNoCommonFigure.message: No figure fits every method; the nearest bands are $1x apart

rFewReviews.message: Few reviews, so the band is widened

rCcuDisagree.message: Player-count cross-check implies a larger launch than the review estimate

rBeyondMeasured.message: Bigger than any game the sales-per-review ratio was measured on; above about $1 reviews it falls by an amount nobody publishes

rBelowMeasured.message: Under $1 copies, which the accuracy benchmark behind this method excluded

rAgree.message: Sources agree within the expected band

mGrossNote.message: What buyers paid, about $1 per copy — before refunds and Valve’s cut.

wTooFewReviews.message: Fewer than $1 reviews. A lifetime estimate from this would be noise, so there is no number to show yet.

wNoReviewData.message: Could not read the review count from this page.

wNoEstimators.message: No method had enough data to produce an estimate.

wNoFollowers.message: No follower count available. Some games use a community group that is not keyed to the app ID.

wFreeToPlay.message: **Free to play.** Revenue comes from in-app purchases and DLC, which no public signal exposes.

wNoPrice.message: Not enough data to run the revenue waterfall.

wReleased.message: Wishlists are consumed by purchases at launch while followers persist, so the ratio no longer holds. The balance typically peaks at 2-4x the pre-launch count, then decays.

nCcuScope.message: This predicts week-one sales, not lifetime units, so it is never averaged into the figure above. It only widens the band when it disagrees.

nOneMethod.message: Only one method had usable data. A second source would narrow this considerably.

nTrendCompare.message: Compared with your visit $1. Stored on this device only.

nDisagreeRoutes.message: These published rules disagree by $1x. Both are shown rather than averaged.

optLede.message: Defaults come from published studies. Change them if you know your own market better — nobody knows your regional split better than you do.

optDiscountHint.message: How much of the catalogue sells below list over the game's life.

optAudienceHint.message: Combined effect of regional pricing and VAT on realised price.

optRefundHint.message: Valve publishes no average and says it varies a lot by game.

optPositionHint.message: Where the pill sits on a store page.

optScaleHint.message: Scales the whole overlay, text and controls together.

optClearHint.message: Follower counts, owner bands and your visit snapshots. Stored on this device only, never transmitted.

optSanity.message: With these settings a developer keeps $1 of the list price per unit. Around 40% is typical for a mixed audience and 45% for a mostly US and EU one. Drifting toward 70% means a deduction is missing.

hintPillItems.message: Order is fixed. An item is skipped when there is no data for it, so nothing shows a dash. Gross is what buyers paid and net what the developer keeps — show either, or both.

footSteamDBHint.message: Open the raw first-party data this panel infers from

optLanguageHint.message: Applies to the overlay and this page. Steam's own text is unaffected.

rRevenueAssumptions.message: Sales band plus the waterfall assumptions

rFollowerRatio.message: All-games median multiplier; the follower ratio spans $1x to $2x

nRecentVsAll.message: $1 of $2 recent reviews are positive. Valve withholds this score until a game has been out 45 days with enough reviews in the window.

nReviewScope.message: All languages, every purchase type. Steam filters the count shown on the page by your language settings, so its figure will be lower.

optRegionAutoNote.message: Each game gets the profile its own reviews point at. This preview has no game to read, so it assumes a mixed audience.

nCcuLatePeak.message: The all-time player peak came $1 days after launch, so it is not a launch peak and the week-one rule does not apply to it.

nCcuNoPeakDate.message: Without a dated player history there is no way to tell a launch peak from a later spike, so the week-one figure is withheld.

nDerivedMark.message: * our own size for an effect the study established but did not measure

nRegionalAuto.message: $1 of reviews come from markets Steam prices below US list, which reads as: $2

nRevenueBand.message: The band is not just the sales range in money: it also covers discounts of $1 to $2 and refunds of $3 to $4.

rWishlistGenre.message: Genre multiplier for $1, inside the measured $2x to $3x range

oSaidOn.message: announced $1, carried forward at the measured growth rate

nWishlistRank.message: Ranked #$1 of $2 · top $3% of announced games

nWishlistBelowList.message: Not in Steam's wishlist ranking, which ends near $1

rWishlistSaid.message: The developer published a figure for this game, so the estimate is mostly that number

rWishlistRankCurve.message: No published figure for this game, so the estimate is read from its place in Steam's wishlist ranking

rWishlistSaidStale.message: The figure the developer published dates from $1, so the ranking carries most of the estimate

rWishlistBelowList.message: Below Steam's wishlist ranking entirely, so only the follower ratio answers

rWishlistRankPending.message: The wishlist ranking has not arrived, so only the follower ratio answers

rWishlistCeiling.message: The follower ratio implies more wishlists than the bottom of a ranking this game is not in

nDlcExcluded.message: Excludes revenue from $1 DLC, which no public signal exposes.

nCommonRegion.message: Every method allows $1 to $2 — that overlap, not the distance between their midpoints, is what agreement means here.

nNoCommonRegion.message: No figure satisfies every method: the nearest ranges are $1x apart, so the band below covers all of them.

rPlaytimeDisagree.message: Player-hours imply a figure outside this band, on an average playtime nobody publishes

nPlaytimeScope.message: From $1 measured player-hours divided by an assumed average playtime. That divisor is the weak link: no public source reports it, and a review sample stands in for it.

rRegionalMeasured.message: Audience mix read from review languages, not assumed

rRegionalAssumed.message: Audience mix is a default; the regional factor spans 0.60 to 0.88

rOwnersNoRecord.message: SteamSpy has no data on file for this game, so there is no second method

rOwnersTooSmall.message: SteamSpy's owner band is too small to trust, so there is no second method

wTypeDemo.message: This is a demo, and Steam names no full game for it. A demo has no sales to estimate.

wTypeDlc.message: This is DLC. The review multiple was measured on base games, and DLC buyers already own the game and have often already reviewed it, so its reviews-per-sale ratio is its own and nobody has published it.

wTypeMusic.message: This is a soundtrack. The review multiple was measured on games, not albums, and nobody has published one for them.

wTypeVideo.message: This is video, not a game. There is nothing here that the sales estimators were measured on.

wTypeHardware.message: This is hardware. It is not sold under the revenue share, so the royalty step does not apply, and no review multiple has ever been measured for devices.

wTypeMod.message: This is a mod, not a game sold on Steam, so there is nothing to estimate.

wTypeAdvertising.message: This is a promotional page rather than a game, so there is nothing to estimate.

wUnsupportedType.message: This store page is not a game. An unfamiliar kind of page is no reason to assume the game multiple applies to it.

nViaDemo.message: You are on the demo page. Every figure here is for the full game.

nDemoReviews.message: Measured on the demo itself. It is not an input to any figure above.
